---
title: "Use the mesh in D-HYDRO"
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import netCDF4
from shapely import Point, box

from refined_quads import generate

workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
quad_mesh = generate(
    box(155_000, 463_000, 155_320, 463_240),
    cell_size=32.0,
    refinement_areas=[(Point(155_160, 463_120).buffer(40), 1)],
    transition_rows=1,
    crs="EPSG:28992",
)
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Do not call it `mesh` next to D-HyDAMO"}
D-HyDAMO scripts usually import `from hydrolib.dhydamo.geometry import mesh` (the module
with `mesh2d_clip`, `links1d2d_add_links_1d_to_2d` and so on). `mesh = generate(...)`
replaces that module, and the next `mesh.<function>(...)` fails with an
`AttributeError`. Use another name, such as `quad_mesh` in the examples here.
:::

## Write a net file

```{python}
#| output: false
from refined_quads import write_ugrid

write_ugrid(quad_mesh, workdir / "mesh_net.nc")
```

The file is UGRID-1.0 with the structure of the D-HYDRO mesh generator export: the
`Mesh2d` topology with nodes, edges and faces, edge and face coordinates and face bounds.
For EPSG:28992 the CRS variable has exactly the attributes of the D-Flow FM plugin; for
another projected CRS they are derived with pyproj; a mesh without CRS gets no CRS
variable.

```{python}
#| echo: false
with netCDF4.Dataset(workdir / "mesh_net.nc") as ds:
    crs = ds["projected_coordinate_system"]
    print("variables:", ", ".join(ds.variables))
    print(f"CRS: {crs.getncattr('name')} (EPSG {crs.getncattr('epsg')})")
```

## Bed levels

The net file has no bed level (no `Mesh2d_node_z` or `Mesh2d_face_z`). Give the bed level
to D-Flow FM as samples: a file `bodem_2d.xyz` with `x y z` on every cell centre, and two
`[Initial]` blocks at the top of the field file (after `[General]`), with
`bedLevType = 1` in the MDU:

```ini
[Initial]
quantity            = bedlevel
dataFile            = bodem_2d.xyz
dataFileType        = sample
interpolationMethod = averaging
operand             = O
averagingType       = nearestNb
averagingRelSize    = 3.0
averagingNumMin     = 1
extrapolationMethod = 0
locationType        = 2d

[Initial]
quantity            = bedlevel
dataFile            = bodem_2d.xyz
dataFileType        = sample
interpolationMethod = averaging
operand             = O
averagingType       = nearestNb
averagingRelSize    = 1.0
averagingNumMin     = 1
extrapolationMethod = 0
locationType        = 2d
```

The first block fills every cell from the nearest sample in a wide area, also cells
that have no sample of their own; the second gives each cell the value on its own
centre. A bed level per cell in the net file does not work in the D-HYDRO GUI: the GUI
rebuilds the cells from nodes and edges and closes small gaps, after which the list no
longer fits the cells and the import fails (see
[ADR-0003](../adr/0003-no-bed-level-in-the-net-file.qmd)). Without samples D-Flow FM uses
`BedLevUni` everywhere, without a warning.

### With D-HyDAMO

When the mesh is read with `mesh2d_from_netcdf` and the bed level comes from a raster
(`mesh2d_altitude_from_raster(network, raster, "face", ...)`), hydrolib writes it as
`mesh2d_face_z`. Turn it into samples around saving the model. Before
`dimr.save(recurse=True)`:

```python
import numpy as np

m2d = fm.geometry.netfile.network._mesh2d
fz = np.asarray(m2d.mesh2d_face_z, dtype=float)
ok = np.isfinite(fz) & (fz > -999)
bodem_xyz = np.column_stack([m2d.mesh2d_face_x, m2d.mesh2d_face_y, fz])[ok]
fm.geometry.bedlevtype = 1
```

After saving: write the samples, remove `mesh2d_face_z` from the net file (netCDF4
cannot delete a variable, so the rest is copied), and put the two blocks above at the
top of the field file:

```python
import os, re
import netCDF4

dfm_dir = Path(output_path) / "dflowfm"
np.savetxt(dfm_dir / "bodem_2d.xyz", bodem_xyz, fmt="%.3f %.3f %.4f")

net = dfm_dir / Path(str(fm.geometry.netfile.filepath)).name
tmp = net.with_name(net.stem + "_tmp.nc")
with netCDF4.Dataset(net) as src, netCDF4.Dataset(tmp, "w", format=src.file_format) as dst:
    for ds in (src, dst):
        ds.set_auto_maskandscale(False)
        ds.set_auto_chartostring(False)
    dst.setncatts(src.__dict__)
    for name, dim in src.dimensions.items():
        dst.createDimension(name, None if dim.isunlimited() else len(dim))
    for name, var in src.variables.items():
        if name.lower() == "mesh2d_face_z":
            continue
        atts = dict(var.__dict__)
        fill = atts.pop("_FillValue", None)
        dst.createVariable(name, var.datatype, var.dimensions, fill_value=fill).setncatts(atts)
        dst[name][...] = var[...]
os.replace(tmp, net)

block = """[Initial]
quantity            = bedlevel
dataFile            = bodem_2d.xyz
dataFileType        = sample
interpolationMethod = averaging
operand             = O
averagingType       = nearestNb
averagingRelSize    = {}
averagingNumMin     = 1
extrapolationMethod = 0
locationType        = 2d

"""
ini = dfm_dir / "fieldFile.ini"
text = ini.read_text() if ini.exists() else "[General]\nfileVersion = 2.00\nfileType    = iniField\n\n"
m = re.search(r"^\[(?!general\])", text, re.M | re.I)  # the first block after [General]
i = m.start() if m else len(text)
ini.write_text(text[:i] + block.format(3.0) + block.format(1.0) + text[i:])

# hydrolib leaves iniFieldFile out of the MDU when the model had no field file
mdu = dfm_dir / Path(str(fm.filepath)).name
t = mdu.read_text()
if not re.search(r"(?im)^\s*iniFieldFile\s*=\s*[^\s#]", t):
    t = re.sub(r"(?im)^\s*iniFieldFile\s*=.*\n", "", t)
    t = re.sub(r"(?im)^(\[geometry\][^\n]*\n)", r"\1iniFieldFile = fieldFile.ini\n", t, count=1)
    mdu.write_text(t)
```

Other bed level blocks in the field file come after these two and overwrite them where
they have values, for example a fixed bed level per polygon.

### Bed level on the nodes

To give the bed level on the nodes instead (`bedLevType` 3 to 6), sample the raster on
the nodes and write it as `mesh2d_node_z`. The nodes do not change when the GUI rebuilds
the cells, so a value per node always fits; no sample file is needed. Before
`dimr.save(recurse=True)`:

```python
import types
import numpy as np

# hydrolib fills NaN's (nodes on the edge, partly outside the raster) in place, but
# pandas 3 returns read-only arrays: let the raster statistics return writable copies
_stats = mesh.rasterstats.raster_stats_fine_cells
if not getattr(_stats, "_writable", False):
    def _writable_stats(*args, **kwargs):
        df = _stats(*args, **kwargs)
        return {c: types.SimpleNamespace(values=df[c].to_numpy(copy=True)) for c in df.columns}
    _writable_stats._writable = True
    mesh.rasterstats.raster_stats_fine_cells = _writable_stats

network = fm.geometry.netfile.network
mesh.mesh2d_altitude_from_raster(network, rasterpath, "node", "mean", fill_option="nearest")
m2d = network._mesh2d
if len(m2d.mesh2d_face_z) != len(m2d.mesh2d_face_x):  # a stale face_z breaks the save
    m2d.mesh2d_face_z = np.empty(0)
fm.geometry.bedlevtype = 3  # 3 mean, 4 minimum, 5 maximum of the node values
```

After saving, remove `mesh2d_face_z` from the net file as above (the block up to
`os.replace(tmp, net)`): hydrolib always writes it, and the GUI reads it and fails on its
rebuilt cells. Leave out the `[Initial] bedlevel` blocks: they would overwrite the nodes.
Tested with D-Flow FM 2026.02: every cell gets a bed level between the lowest and the
highest of its node values.

### Which bedLevType

"Face" means two opposite things here. In the net file (UGRID 1.0) a face is a **cell**:
`mesh2d_face_z` is a level per cell. In the description of `bedLevType` in the MDU,
"at face" means at a **cell side** through which water flows (a flow link or u-point),
the finite-volume meaning. This table uses cell, cell side and node only.

| `bedLevType` | Input | Level of a cell side | Bed level of the cell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | per cell: samples (or `mesh2d_face_z`) | not measured (MDU: the higher of the two cells) | the cell's own value |
| 2 | per cell side: samples | the sample | not measured |
| 3 | per node: `mesh2d_node_z` | mean of its two nodes | the lowest of its cell sides |
| 4 | per node | the lower of its two nodes | the lowest of its cell sides, so its lowest node |
| 5 | per node | the higher of its two nodes | the lowest of its cell sides |
| 6 | per node | not measured | mean of its nodes |

Only cell sides shared with another cell count; sides on the edge of the mesh do not.
The cell formulas were measured with D-Flow FM 2026.02 on a mesh of 849 cells: each
matches the bed level D-Flow FM uses in every cell to 0.1 mm. In short: 1 gives each
cell exactly its own value; 6 the mean of its nodes; 4 its lowest node; with 3 and 5 one
low cell side makes the whole cell low.

::: {.callout-note title="Net files written by refined-quads 0.1.x"}
These contain `Mesh2d_node_z` with -999. After a clip with MeshKernel that array keeps
its old length and saving fails with "shape mismatch". Before saving, empty it:
`if len(m2d.mesh2d_node_z) != len(m2d.mesh2d_node_x): m2d.mesh2d_node_z = np.empty(0)`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="GeoTIFF fields in the D-HYDRO GUI"}
The GUI only reads rasters with the extension `.tif` (or `.asc`); with `.tiff` it stops
at "reading spatial operations". D-Flow FM and DIMR read both.
:::

## Read a net file

`read_ugrid` reads only the 2D mesh of a net file; a 1D network and other variables in it
are ignored. The lattice is derived from the square cells, so you can check or refine a
mesh from any program:

```{python}
from refined_quads import check, read_ugrid

quad_mesh = read_ugrid(workdir / "mesh_net.nc")
print(check(quad_mesh).summary())
```

## If the orthogonality repair does not close

D-Flow FM rejects a network whose edges are not orthogonal enough. The generator repairs
such edges; if that does not close, `generate` raises `OrthogonalityRepairError` with the
raw mesh (`exc.mesh`) and the problem locations (`exc.bad_points`), and the command line
writes `<output>_raw.nc` and `<output>_problems.gpkg` next to the output so you can look
at them in QGIS.
